budget_items.topic: PFAS/manganese testing of four wells feeding Well 5

budget_items.topic: Metal Lane water main pipe material (plastic vs. ductile)

budget_items.topic: Saddle fittings for plastic pipe taps
budget_items.what_was_said: Tapping the new plastic water main requires a saddle fitting costing around $100 each, an added but modest expense compared to a direct tap.

minutes.headline: Water Commissioners tabled a quarterly water-quality reporting plan and approved the annual audit contract
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District Commissioners reviewed warrants and minutes, addressed a resident association's kayak rack relocation near the wellfield, and went through sampling results showing manganese/iron/PFAS issues at several wells. They authorized the chair to sign the annual audit agreement with Mark Mueller, discussed the completed Metal Lane water main replacement and its choice of plastic pipe, and held off on a proposal to publish quarterly water-quality charts on the website pending cost details from vendors.

what_happened.line: Commissioners approved the annual audit engagement, authorizing the chair to sign the agreement with the auditor.
They tabled a plan to publish quarterly manganese, iron and PFAS results on the district website until vendors provide cost details.
They chose to wait until the October sampling round to test the wells feeding Well 5 rather than test twice, to save money.
Commissioners agreed to send a letter confirming a kayak rack's relocation away from the wellfield is currently allowed under district bylaws.
The completed Metal Lane water main replacement used plastic pipe, a choice discussed for its cost and performance versus ductile pipe.

why_it_matters: The audit keeps the district's required annual financial review on schedule, and the contracted fee is described as higher than last year, though the exact figure is from captions and not restated as fact here.
Whether quarterly water-quality data appears on the website affects how directly residents can track manganese, iron and PFAS results by well rather than learning of them only at meetings.
The pipe-material choice on the finished water main and the decision to delay well testing until October both touch what the project and ongoing monitoring cost the district.
